transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, hi. Um… I guess the main thing is my focus has gotten kind of hard to manage. I’m a software developer, and lately I’ll be fixing something simple, like a rendering bug, and then a Slack ping or even some color pattern on the screen—or a siren outside—just pulls me into a totally different idea before I finish the line of code.

It’s not that I’m trying to be careless or anything. I can usually handle distractions, but this feels more… slippery, I guess. I’m not sure if that’s the right way to explain it.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

Yeah… a bit. I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it fidgeting exactly, but sitting still has been hard. I wake up already sort of… mentally moving, planning features, code changes, even bigger picture stuff like layouts or how things should be presented.

So when I’m just sitting there, it feels like I’m wasting time somehow. Like there’s this current pushing me to get up and do the next thing. Is that the kind of restlessness you mean?
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Sometimes, yeah… I mean, I usually try to be thoughtful, and I don’t want to make it sound like I’m reckless all the time.

But there were a couple things recently that… probably fit. I spent money we hadn’t really agreed on—GPUs, some print materials, promo videos—because in the moment it felt like we had to move fast. And I pushed an update without getting the usual approval because waiting for another review cycle honestly felt like the whole opportunity would just die.

I know that probably doesn’t sound great. At the time it felt necessary, but afterward I could see why people were upset.
Have these difficulties with focus and impulsivity caused problems for you at work or in your personal relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say it hasn’t, but… it has, unfortunately.

Work put me on leave after I bypassed the approval process and deployed those changes myself. I think they saw it as a serious judgment issue, which… I understand, even if at the time I thought I was helping.

And at home, my wife’s been pretty upset. She says the spending and the arguments around it have made things feel unstable. I don’t want to make it sound like everything is falling apart, but it’s definitely caused strain. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been experiencing any significant mood swings or irritability lately?

Yeah… I guess there have been some swings, or maybe more like I’ve been running hotter than usual.

Most days I feel really energized—kind of lit up, like things are finally clicking and Glendale is finally catching up to what I’ve been trying to build. And that feels good, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m out of control.

But… I do get irritated pretty fast when my wife or people at work slow things down with what they call “process.” I know process matters, I do. It’s just in the moment it feels like they’re blocking something important, and I can snap harder than I mean to. Does that make sense?
Do you experience these difficulties with focus and impulsivity at home or in social situations, not just at work?

Yeah… not only at work. I mean, it shows up more clearly there because coding makes it obvious, but it happens at home too.

What really brought me in is that I can’t seem to keep my mind on one thing the way I used to. I’ll be trying to fix a rendering bug, and then a Slack ping comes in, or I notice a color pattern, or even a siren outside goes by, and suddenly I’m off into some whole new idea before I’ve even finished the line of code I was on.

I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s been… harder to stay anchored, I guess. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you find it difficult to focus and stay on task when you're not working, like when you're relaxing or on vacation?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I’d like to say it’s just a work thing because that sounds more manageable, but it’s kind of the same pattern when I’m supposed to be relaxing.

My attention just doesn’t stay put very well. Like even when I’m trying to do something simple, my mind catches on some little thing—a sound outside, a pattern I notice, a notification—and suddenly I’m off chasing another idea before I’ve finished what I was doing.

It’s not constant every second, but it’s enough that I’ve noticed it. Is that what you mean?
Do you experience these difficulties with focus and impulsivity consistently, even on weekends or days off?

Yeah… I think it’s pretty consistent. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, like I’m completely unable to function, but even on days off my mind doesn’t really settle.

The thing that brought me in is just… I can’t keep my mind on one thing the way I used to. At work it’s obvious—like I’ll be fixing a rendering bug, and then a Slack ping comes in, or I notice some color pattern, or even a siren outside goes by, and suddenly I’m pulled into a whole new idea before I’ve even finished the line I was on.

Weekends are maybe less structured, so it’s harder to measure, but it still happens. Does that make sense?
Did you have difficulties with focus or impulsivity when you were a child?

Um… I’m not really sure. I don’t remember it being a big issue when I was a kid, at least not in the way it feels now.

I mean, I probably got distracted like any kid, but I don’t have a clear memory of teachers or my parents saying it was a serious problem. I did okay in school overall, so… I don’t know if that counts. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Did you have any difficulties with paying attention or sitting still in school when you were a child?

Not that I can really remember, no. I mean, I wasn’t the perfect student or anything, but I don’t have memories of constantly being in trouble for not paying attention or not sitting still.

I got through school okay, and I don’t remember teachers making it a big issue. My parents didn’t really talk about it that way either, at least as far as I know.

I’m sorry, I know that’s probably not the most helpful answer… I just don’t want to guess and say yes if I’m not sure.
Did you experience any symptoms like these when you were an adolescent?

I don’t think so, at least not in any obvious way. As a teenager I was probably distracted sometimes, like with homework or classes I didn’t care about, but I don’t remember it standing out as a real problem.

I wasn’t getting constant complaints from teachers or anything like that, and I don’t think I was especially impulsive compared to other kids. I mean, I could be forgetting some things, but nothing comes to mind that feels like what I’m dealing with now. Is that helpful?
Did your parents or teachers ever mention that you had trouble paying attention or controlling your impulses when you were growing up?

Not really, no… at least not that I remember. I don’t think my parents or teachers ever sat me down or said I had a problem with attention or impulse control.

I’m sure I had normal kid moments, but nothing that was pointed out as concerning. I did okay overall, so I guess it just never stood out. I hope that answers it okay.
Did your difficulties with focus and impulsivity start when you were a child or are they a more recent development?

I’d say it’s more recent. I don’t really remember this being a childhood thing.

It’s been going on for maybe about three months now… since my platform was selected for the Glendale showcase. I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s when I started noticing the focus and impulsivity stuff more. Does that make sense?
Have your difficulties with focus and impulsivity been present for at least six months?

No, I don’t think it’s been six months. It’s more like… about three months, since my platform was selected for the Glendale showcase.

I mean, it feels like a noticeable stretch of time, but not six months. I hope that’s clear.
Have your difficulties with focus and impulsivity been persistent?

It’s been kind of persistent, yes… but only for about three months or so, since my platform was selected for the Glendale showcase. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it hasn’t really just gone away during that time. Does that answer what you mean by persistent?
Have your difficulties with focus and impulsivity been present for at least six months, or have they been consistently problematic over a shorter period?

Right, yes — I think the more accurate way to say it is it’s been consistently a problem, but over a shorter period. About three months, really, since my platform was selected for the Glendale showcase.

So not six months. I just want to be precise about that.
Have you noticed any periods where your symptoms of difficulty with focus and impulsivity significantly improved or went away since they started?

Not really, no. I mean, it hasn’t been years or anything — it’s been about three months, since my platform was selected for the Glendale showcase — but during that stretch I can’t say it fully went away.

There may be better days, sure, but overall it’s been kind of consistently there. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have you had any periods where you didn't experience these difficulties with focus and impulsivity since they started about three months ago?

No, I don’t think there’s been a real stretch where it just wasn’t there. I mean, I’ve had better moments, but since it started — about three months ago, when my platform got selected for the Glendale showcase — it’s kind of been around. Maybe not terrible every single day, but present.
Have you experienced significant difficulties with focus and impulsivity for less than six months?
Yes, less than six months. It’s been about three months, since my platform was selected for the Glendale showcase. I know I’ve said that a few times — I just want to be accurate and not overstate it.
Have you experienced any significant reduction in symptoms when you're not under stress or pressure to perform?

Maybe a little? I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But even when I’m not under a big deadline or anything, it’s still there.

Like, I’ll be fixing a rendering bug, and then a Slack ping comes in, or I notice some color pattern, or even a siren outside, and suddenly my brain is off on a whole different idea before I’ve finished the line of code. So pressure probably doesn’t help, but I don’t think it fully settles down just because the pressure is off. Does that answer it?
